task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) hard gate on REQ-161's design at lib/letflow/design/req161-lua-platform-fail.md. CODE-DESIGNER's central claim: platform.fail terminates via exit({:script_failed, %{reason:, details:}}) instead of raise, because REQ-148's spike answer (b) found host-raised errors ARE pcall-catchable, and deps/lua's pcall/xpcall implementations only rescue (never catch :exit). Independently re-verify this claim against the real vendored Lua library source -- do not trust the design doc's own account. Also verify the SCRIPT_FAILED-vs-SCRIPT_ERROR distinction, the honest gap disclosures (executor.ex's handle_yield_result/3 stringifying the exit reason today; no engine-side dispatch call site yet), and that platform.fail remains ungated (required: :none, unedited).
acceptance_criteria: Independently read deps/lua/lib/lua/vm/stdlib.ex's lua_pcall/2 and lua_xpcall/2, and the native-function dispatch path (do_call_function/3 or equivalent), and confirm directly that they only `rescue` and never `catch :exit` -- do not take the design's citation at face value, read the real source lines yourself.

Confirm exit({:script_failed, %{reason:, details:}}) is not one of Elixir/OTP's reserved exit-reason rewrite atoms (:kill, :normal, :shutdown) that would be silently transformed or swallowed -- verify against real OTP semantics.
Confirm the structured payload genuinely survives to a real monitor via :DOWN delivery, unmodified -- not assumed.

Confirm SCRIPT_FAILED ({:script_failed, %{...}}) and any plausible future SCRIPT_ERROR shape (a normal Lua.eval!/2 return carrying a Lua.RuntimeException, per the design) are structurally non-collapsible -- one is a process-exit signal, the other a normal return value; verify this claim's logic holds.

Confirm the design's own disclosed gap (executor.ex's handle_yield_result/3 stringifies any exit reason today, so the SCRIPT_FAILED/SCRIPT_ERROR distinction is only provable at the raw task/monitor boundary, not through Executor) is accurately stated, not overstated or understated -- read handle_yield_result/3's real code.
Confirm platform.fail's capability_matrix row is unedited (required: :none) -- no capability gate was added.
All 7 real acceptance criteria in docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-161 entry mapped to concrete design elements in a traceability table.
Zero literal Elixir code anywhere in the design doc -- @spec/@type only.
